D=∏_(t=0)^(λ.toNat) c_t; an empty product is one.
U=V(K)=M⊗_Z K, the balanced tensor product of integer modules. Its K-action is a·(m⊗b)=m⊗(ab).

This notation asserts no preservation of M by an arbitrary T; preservation must be established in the packet. inputs.statement: p is an arbitrary prime, K is an arbitrary field with Char K=p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.
For every j with 0≤j≤λ the integer c_j=binom(λ,j) has nonzero image in K; for every r with 0≤r≤λ the integer r! has nonzero image in K. Hence D=∏_(j=0)^λ c_j also has nonzero image in K.

Let A_ij^K denote the operator induced by A_ij|_M on U=M⊗_Z K and define F_ij=(c_j in K)^(-1) A_ij^K for 0≤i,j≤λ. Then F_ij F_kl=δ_(jk)F_il and Σ_(i=0)^λ F_ii=Id_U. For 0≤r≤λ the induced divided powers satisfy (r! in K)X_r^K=(x^K)^r and (r! in K)Y_r^K=(y^K)^r.

binders.type: K-linear operator family defined by F_ij=(c_j in K)^(-1) A_ij^K, where the A_ij^K are the induced operators specified in this statement

argument.text: N007 establishes that x,y,h and every X_r,Y_r preserve M and have integer-linear restrictions, so every one of their induced operators in D009 is defined. N004 supplies A_ij^K and the family F_ij=(c_j in K)^(-1)A_ij^K. N003 supplies the nonzero coefficients in this formula. By H001 the indices 0≤i,j≤λ have λ−i,λ−j,λ all within 0,…,λ.

produces.statement: The induced x,y,h,X_r,Y_r are well-defined on U for every natural r. For all 0≤i,j≤λ the three orders λ−i, λ, λ−j in A_ij lie between 0 and λ.

argument.text: Fix W and introduce L1: W is invariant under x^K,y^K,h^K. Invariance under x^K and y^K implies invariance under every power of these operators, by induction on the exponent with identity as base and composition as step. For each 0≤r≤λ, N003 gives r!≠0 in K, and N004 gives X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)(x^K)^r and Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)(y^K)^r. A K-subspace is closed under scalar multiples, so it is invariant under all these X_r^K,Y_r^K.

produces.statement: W is invariant under X_r^K and Y_r^K for every 0≤r≤λ.

argument.text: For every i,j in the range, D006 and the induced tensor formula imply A_ij^K=X_(λ−i)^K Y_λ^K X_λ^K Y_(λ−j)^K. Indeed the right side applied to a pure tensor m⊗a is (X_(λ−i)Y_λX_λY_(λ−j)m)⊗a, the defining action of the left side; N007 guarantees every intermediate lattice vector stays in M, and pure tensors span U. F001 and F002 therefore show W is invariant under A_ij^K. Scalar closure then shows W invariant under F_ij=c_j^(-1)A_ij^K. The h-invariance premise has no further use.

produces.statement: W is invariant under every F_ij=(c_j in K)^(-1)(X_(λ−i)Y_λX_λY_(λ−j))^K for 0≤i,j≤λ.

argument.text: Discharge L1. For the arbitrary K-subspace W, invariance under the induced x,y,h therefore implies invariance under all the displayed F_ij. Universal introduction in W proves the output statement exactly, with all induced maps already constructed in S001.
